meals.description: Two hamburger patties, half serving of rice, egg, two servings of broccoli, seaweed soup with two fish/meat balls, and light sauce.
meals.note: Re-estimated item by item on 2026-09-15. Supersedes the earlier 1,080 kcal meal estimate; not an additional meal. All portions are assumptions unless explicitly reported.

items.name: Hamburger patties
assumptions: Assumes 125 g cooked per patty and an 85%-lean ground-beef reference. Neither weight nor fat percentage was measured.
Reference per 100 g: 250 kcal, 25.93 g protein, 15.41 g fat. Restaurant binders and oil could change this.
items.tip: Ask for the patty weight or lean percentage next time; that would tighten the largest uncertainty in this meal.

items.name: Half portion of rice
items.portion: Half the bowl eaten · assumed 110 g cooked
assumptions: The photo shows the full bowl. Only half is counted, following your correction.
Assumes 110 g cooked white rice; reference is 130 kcal, 2.69 g protein, 28.17 g carbs and 0.28 g fat per 100 g. Egg and sauce have separate cards.
items.tip: Keep the portion comfortable for your appetite; add vegetables rather than treating rice as something you must eliminate.

items.name: Soft egg
assumptions: Uses a poached-egg reference as a proxy for the soft egg. No added butter or oil included.
Per 100 g: 143 kcal, 12.51 g protein, 0.71 g carbs and 9.47 g fat.
items.tip: The egg contributes protein. Any oil or extra sauce should be recorded separately.

items.name: Double broccoli
assumptions: Includes the extra broccoli you reported and very little sauce. Assumes no added cooking oil.
Cooked broccoli reference per 100 g: 35 kcal, 2.38 g protein, 7.18 g carbs, 0.41 g fat and 3.3 g fiber.
items.tip: Keep the extra vegetables. They add volume and fiber alongside the rest of the meal.

items.name: Two soup balls
assumptions: The exact fish/meat mixture, filling and brand are unknown. This is a proxy, not a product identification.
Uses a 50 g portion of a fish-roe-ball label (205 kcal, 12.5 g protein, 8.7 g carbs, 13.4 g fat per 100 g). Plain fish balls or meat balls can differ substantially.

sources.title: Example fish-ball product label, not the confirmed product

items.tip: A menu name or ingredient label would make this estimate much more useful.

items.name: Seaweed broth
assumptions: Recipe is unknown. A working allowance of 1 g protein, 3 g carbs and 1 g fat is used for a light seaweed broth.
This is an explicit recipe assumption, not a database measurement. The two soup balls are counted separately. Sodium cannot be estimated reliably from the photo.
items.tip: If the broth tastes salty, you can enjoy the solids without needing to finish all the broth.

items.name: Light dipping sauces
assumptions: Models about 10 g carbohydrate from the lightly used sauces. Exact amount and recipe are unknown.
This assumes mostly sweet/soy-based sauces, not a mayonnaise-based sauce. Bottles shown are reference photos and are not extra servings.
items.tip: Keeping sauce on the side makes the amount you actually use easier to notice and log.

meals.description: Two medium M Stand iced Americanos, black, no milk or sugar, around 17:00.

items.name: M Stand Americanos
assumptions: You confirmed M Stand black iced Americanos with no milk or sugar. Both medium cups are counted once.
Uses two 15-kcal plain iced Americano servings as a working proxy (1 g protein and 2 g carbs each). This is not a verified M Stand nutrition label.
Actual cup volume and espresso shots are unknown. Caffeine is left unknown; plain black coffee contributes little energy.

sources.title: Starbucks plain iced Americano nutrition — proxy, not M Stand’s recipe

items.tip: Black coffee avoids calories from milk and syrups. Notice whether two late coffees affect your sleep; decaf or an earlier coffee are options.

assumptions: The photo is included in the diary. There is no confirmed amount drunk or fruit eaten, so it is excluded from totals.
references.tip: If you drank some or ate the fruit, log the amount and it can be added.

suggestions.title: Keep the vegetable boost
suggestions.text: You added a second serving of broccoli. At another meal, try a mix of vegetables and fruit alongside protein and a grain; no need to skip a meal to compensate for this one.

suggestions.title: Make the next estimate easier
suggestions.text: The patties dominate the calorie uncertainty. A cooked weight or menu description would help more than trying to guess every trace of sauce.

suggestions.title: Check the 5 p.m. coffees
suggestions.text: Your two M Stand Americanos were black, with no milk or sugar. If a 5 p.m. coffee affects sleep, consider an earlier coffee, a smaller serving or decaf. Caffeine depends on the number of espresso shots.

methodology: Working estimates, not measured nutrition. Source values are scaled to explicitly stated portion assumptions; recipe proxies are labelled. Incomplete days and pending foods are never zero-filled.
